newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi Kurds say Baghdad readies new front.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds say Baghdad readies new front.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish group said on Saturday that Iraq was moving tanks into a position that would place the Kurdish faction under attack from three fronts around their Sulaimaniya stronghold.

Iraq joined the fighting in northern Iraq a week ago on the side of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) to kick the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) out of the main northern Iraqi Kurdish city of Arbil.

"Iraq attacked and shelled Arbil and our positions in the region with 500 tanks and are now moving 200 of them to the south," Jabbar Farman, commander of the PUK peshmerga and former defence minister of the Kurdish adminstration, said on Saturday.
Sulaimaniya, 120 km (72 miles) south of Arbil, is the last major northern Iraqi settlement still in PUK hands. The KDP and PUK have been fighting for decades.

Residents of Sulaimaniya have largely pinned their hopes on Washington, which retaliated for Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's thrust into northern Iraq by sending two volleys of cruise missiles into southern Iraq last week.
"After invading Arbil, Iraq and the KDP moved towards Chamchamal. It was the first front towards Sulaimaniya," Farman told Reuters.

"The second front was opened in this region with Wednesday night attacks. This Degala-Koi Sanjak route leads to the region's main electricity power supplier, the Dukan dam, and then Sulaimaniya is the target," he said.

Farman said starting on Wednesday, Iraq began to move 200 of its tanks and 155mm artillery from the Arbil area to the third front he said they want to open, towards the second passage through the mountains to the south of Sulaimaniya.

Osman Haji Mahmoud, commander of the regional PUK forces in the Chamchamal area, said KDP forces had failed to gain new positions despite support from Iraqi shelling. PUK commanders said 11 of their fighters were killed and 20 wounded in the fighting.
Kurdish groups in the Bestana-Degala region agreed to break off their fighting to let U.N. technicians fix a power line on Sunday cut during the clashes, a United Nations official said.
The power lines, running from Sulaimaniya to Arbil and the KDP-held city of Salahuddin, were destroyed during the Iraqi shelling of Arbil and other positions of the PUK.
"People in Arbil and Salahuddin and Shaqlawa region suffer from lack of electricity and water supply," Bent Blankenstein, U.N. senior communications officer, told Reuters.

Heavy fighting kept U.N. technical teams from making the repairs for three days, he said. The KDP stopped shelling on Saturday to let the teams through and the PUK agreed to allow the work to begin at 10 a.m (0600 GMT) on Sunday.
